queue_items.claim: The sole warrant against dividing the chapter is an exclusivity claim that no fresh time-frame or scene turn recurs inside the span, and two such devices stand in the span's own bytes - one of them spliced by the row itself.
queue_items.grounds: boundary_rationale ends by asserting that no new narrative-onset marker, a fresh time-frame or scene turn, recurs to divide the unit; no digit-bearing sweep citation accompanies it, and the universals checker flags exactly this clause (the only universals flag across the eight rows of this slice). The row's own byte-tier splice from oshb:Isa.20.2 opens בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא (byte tier), a verse-initial time frame that stands at only 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, oshb:Isa.18.7 and oshb:Isa.20.2). A second scene-turn device stands verse-internally at oshb:Isa.20.6: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ (byte tier), one of 45 verses carrying that onset book-wide (sweep: 45 verses, skeleton tier) - and one of the seven sites beyond its own span that the row covering Isa.19.16-Isa.19.25 counts when it makes that same device its structuring driver across chapters 19-24. The interior seam the row does argue against, at Isa.20.2|Isa.20.3 before the divine-speech onset וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.20.3, byte tier), is also exactly where the single-witness setumah the inventory records at Isa.20.2 falls. The whole-chapter reading remains defensible on content and the confidence already sits at the whole-chapter cap; the warrant as written does not survive its own bytes.
queue_items.proposed_change: Replace the undigited exclusivity clause with a digit-bearing formulation that names and disposes of both interior sites - the Isa.20.2 time frame and the Isa.20.6 scene turn. No span change proposed.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: This chapter is a single sign-act report bounded by its own narrative onset, “In the year that Tartan came to Ashdod” (web:Isa.20.1), and the command frame "בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ בְּיַ֣ד יְשַׁעְיָ֣הוּ" (oshb:Isa.20.2, byte tier) -- a time-frame and messenger clause continuing, in the same verse, into an imperative to strip off sackcloth and sandals and the compliance clause reporting it done, “He did so, walking naked and barefoot.” (web:Isa.20.2). The interpretation opens with its own divine-speech onset, "וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה" (oshb:Isa.20.3, byte tier), “Yahweh said,” (web:Isa.20.3); the servant reference naming the sign-actor is explicit rather than one of the unnamed servant-figure zones elsewhere in the book: "עַבְדִּ֥י יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ" (oshb:Isa.20.3, byte tier), "my servant Isaiah," names the prophet himself, “As my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot three years for a sign and a wonder concerning Egypt and concerning Ethiopia,” (web:Isa.20.3). Although narrated in the third person from start to finish rather than as a first-person report, the whole chapter is held as one row bounded by the sign-act's own narrative frame: the divine-speech onset at Isa.20.3 does not open a fresh narrative episode but supplies that same episode's own explanation of the sign already performed and completed in Isa.20.2, and no new narrative-onset marker -- a fresh time-frame or scene turn -- recurs to divide it.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading this unit as narrative_prose parallel to the later court narrative is a defensible alternative label to vision_report, since the whole account is third-person past-tense narration of a sign-act rather than a first-person vision report; the operative-category deviation is disclosed here rather than argued away.

queue_items.grounds: boundary_rationale states 'the watchman noun repeats at skeleton tier while the night-forms that follow it differ at every tier'. Spliced from MT 21:11, the two watchman nouns are "שֹׁמֵר֙" (token 6) and "שֹׁמֵ֖ר" (token 9): consonants and vowel points are identical and only the cantillation differs (U+0599 borne after the resh in the first, U+0596 borne on the mem in the second), so they collate accent_stripped-equal, i.e. the strongest matching tier is accent_stripped, not skeleton. The paired claim about the night-forms is correct: "מִלַּ֔יְלָה" and "מִלֵּֽיל" collate at no tier against each other. Under the tier-disclosure standard the named tier must be the collate truth, and byte / accent_stripped / skeleton are never conflated.

queue_items.claim: The row's declared opening driver is an in-that-day scene shift resting on a formula that is not verse-initial at the cited verse and that recurs byte-identically across the row's own seams, none of it disclosed; the immediately preceding shipped row argues the opposite about this same formula at this same seam.
queue_items.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'opens the unit on an explicit in-that-day scene shift', and observed_substrate_signals leads with oracle_frame.scene_shift, so the day formula is the declared operative signal. Spliced from source, MT 22:12 opens "וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא" — the formula "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא" is the fifth and sixth words, not verse-initial. The same formula stands at MT 22:8 as "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא" (four verses back, inside the immediately preceding row's span Isa.22.1-Isa.22.11), collating accent_stripped-equal against the MT 22:12 form, and at MT 22:20 as the tail of "וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא", where it is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the MT 22:12 form, and again verse-initially at MT 22:25 (accent_stripped against MT 22:12). The row discloses none of these recurrences. The immediately preceding row's device_notes rules on this exact seam that 'The in-that-day formula itself is cross-seam cohesion rather than a boundary driver ... it is verse-initial at neither of the two sites bordering this row's own seam. The warrant for the cut rests instead on the fresh grammatical subject entering at oshb:Isa.22.12' — a warrant this row's observed_substrate_signals does not carry.
queue_items.proposed_change: Re-declare the operative opening signal as the fresh divine grammatical subject entering at oshb:Isa.22.12 (the finite verb with the stacked title as its subject, the first such in the header-bounded oracle), matching the preceding row's ruling; demote the in-that-day formula to disclosed cross-seam cohesion naming oshb:Isa.22.8 (accent_stripped), oshb:Isa.22.20 (byte) and oshb:Isa.22.25 (accent_stripped); add oshb:Isa.22.8 to boundary_evidence_refs; swap the lead observed_substrate_signals key off oracle_frame.scene_shift accordingly, and re-open confidence and strongest_rejected_alternative as dependent fields of the driver swap. Span Isa.22.12-Isa.22.14 unchanged; no span change proposed.

The stacked title opening the unit, אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת (oshb:Isa.22.12, byte tier), and the stacked title closing it, אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Isa.22.14, byte tier), recur at skeleton tier only relative to each other — every token differs in its accent — so the close is read as a repeated frame element rather than a self-contained inclusio.

queue_items.claim: The row's closing-seam warrant — that the following verse opens on its own addressee shift and is a verse-initial addressee-specific commission — is byte-false: MT 22:20 carries no imperative, no vocative and no second-person form at all, and the addressee is unchanged across the seam.
queue_items.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'The row stops before the following verse's own in-that-day summons of a different, newly named servant, which opens the next unit on its own addressee shift'; device_notes: 'the cut still stands on the verse-initial addressee-specific commission opening the following verse, naming a different steward for installation rather than removal.' Spliced from source, MT 22:20 reads "וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְקָרָ֣אתִי לְעַבְדִּ֔י לְאֶלְיָקִ֖ים בֶּן חִלְקִיָּֽהוּ": the newly named steward is governed by the prefixed preposition as the object of the first-person verb, and the verse contains zero second-person forms. It is therefore neither a commission nor an addressee shift — contrast this row's own opening at MT 22:15, whose commission is carried by the imperatives "לֶךְ בֹּא֙". The addressee is in fact unchanged across the seam: the 2ms chain closing this row's span, "וַהֲדַפְתִּ֖יךָ מִמַּצָּבֶ֑ךָ וּמִמַּעֲמָֽדְךָ֖ יֶהֶרְסֶֽךָ" (oshb:Isa.22.19, byte tier), resumes one verse past the seam at "כֻּתָּנְתֶּ֗ךָ וְאַבְנֵֽטְךָ֙" (oshb:Isa.22.21, byte tier). The row states this counter-fact itself in device_notes ('A second-person-masculine-singular address chain crosses this unit's own closing seam ... resumes the direct address'), so the row contradicts itself; and the neighbouring shipped row that owns MT 22:20 reads the same bytes correctly, as a referent brought in 'as the object of the divine verb rather than as a fresh addressee', with 'the grammatical addressee carried over from the removal oracle ... still the one addressed one verse later'. The row ships at high confidence and observed_substrate_signals carries oracle_frame.addressee_shift.
queue_items.proposed_change: Replace the closing-seam warrant with the two signals that do stand in MT 22:20's own bytes and that the neighbouring row already argues: the verse-initial day-formula scene onset and the fresh named referent entering as the object of the divine verb rather than as a fresh addressee. Strike 'addressee shift' and 'addressee-specific commission' from the closing-seam prose; retain oracle_frame.addressee_shift only for this row's OPENING at oshb:Isa.22.15, whose imperatives do carry it; add oshb:Isa.22.20 to boundary_evidence_refs (only oshb:Isa.22.21 is presently carried for that side). As a driver swap this re-opens confidence, strongest_rejected_alternative and observed_substrate_signals. The seam itself survives on the replacement warrant, so no span change is proposed.
